headline: Software rout and blue-chip losses sink Dow 1.6%, S&P −1.0% before Nvidia beat
summary: Stocks slipped from the open and the losses deepened into the afternoon, leaving the S&P 500 and Nasdaq with a fourth straight decline and the S&P 500 at its lowest close since July, while the Dow shed nearly 850 points. Selling was broad — decliners beat advancers by more than 3-to-1 on the NYSE and the Russell 2000 fell 1.5% — but chips steadied: Nvidia pared a drop of nearly 4% to −0.4% and the iShares semiconductor ETF finished slightly higher.
drivers: Software sell-off ahead of Anthropic's IPO

Application-software stocks were the heaviest drag as investors weighed AI disruption risk a day before Anthropic prices its IPO (range kept at $70–78, trading from Thu): Salesforce −9.5%, Intuit and ServiceNow about −7%, Microsoft −2.3% and the IGV software ETF down more than 3%.
Dow blue chips hit across sectors

Beyond Salesforce, Nike fell 6.3% (reversing an early gain on its long-term targets), UnitedHealth 5.4% as health insurers slid, IBM 4.7%, JPMorgan 2.4% after naming a new CFO, and Home Depot 2.5% after a Q3 beat came with a soft outlook and a CEO change.
Nvidia nerves, then a beat after the bell

Nvidia closed −0.4% after falling nearly 4% intraday, helped late by Jensen Huang saying he would return as CEO if the board asked; Broadcom +2.5% and Marvell +2% offset Micron −0.9%. After the close Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8B (vs about $109B expected) and guided Q4 to $130B ±3% (vs about $125B), though with gross margin guided down to 71–72%; the stock rose 2–3% after hours.

St. Louis Fed's Musalem said several more hikes may be needed before spring 2027, keeping a December hike about 95–98% priced; October retail sales rose 0.2% as expected, with the ex-autos-and-gas measure up 0.6% (vs 0.4%). The 10-year yield still eased about 2bp to 5.10% as money left stocks, while the VIX jumped 11% to about 25.5.
week: Two sessions in, the S&P 500 is down 2.9%, the Nasdaq 3.2% and the Dow 3.0% for the week, with Nvidia down 16% since the start of last week and the 10-year yield holding above 5% on expectations of more Fed hikes.
watch: Next: the market's reaction to Nvidia's results and outlook, Fed minutes and Anthropic's IPO pricing on Wed Nov 18, Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and Walmart's results on Thu Nov 19, and the Fed meeting on Dec 8–9.
